observations: Photos 0, 1 and 2: one horizontal foot mounted cycloidal gear reducer with a cast iron housing, lying on a tiled floor; dealer watermark 'IFABROS INDUSTRIAL'.
Large round input flange on one end for bolting a motor; no motor is attached.
Output shaft on the other end covered by a yellow cap or yellow paint; lifting eye and two breather or fill plugs on top.
The whole unit, bolts included, is freshly painted bright blue, so it has been repainted after assembly; the paint hides the original finish and any wear.
No nameplate, rating plate, ratio or brand is visible in any photo.
No oil level, input shaft or turning test is shown.

identity.kind: cycloidal gear reducer, foot mounted, cast iron, no motor
read_from: photo 0 cycloidal housing, feet and output shaft
photo 1 side view with motor flange

claims.evidence: Photos 0 to 2 show a cycloidal speed reducer with motor flange and output shaft.
Photos 0 to 2 show a cast iron housing and feet.
No nameplate or rating plate is visible; rating and ratio cannot be read.
No label, plate or document shows origin; the fresh blue paint over every bolt suggests local refurbishment.
No clip of the shaft turning under power or by hand.
Noise can only be judged with it running.
A gear reducer has no mileage record; nothing in the photos shows hours of use.
The whole unit including bolt heads is repainted, which hides any sign of it having been opened.

risks.risk: Rating and ratio unknown; it may be smaller than the claimed 15 to 20hp
risks.proof: Photo of the nameplate or rating plate, or the housing measured with a tape and the shaft diameter measured
risks.if_unproven: priced as the smallest size seen, of unknown rating

risks.risk: Worn cycloidal discs, pins or bearings hidden under fresh paint
risks.proof: Clip of the input turned by hand or by motor with the output shaft turning smoothly and no backlash
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working, for rebuild or scrap

risks.risk: Repaint may hide cracks or welded repairs on the housing or feet
risks.proof: Close photos of the feet and flange edges
Photo of the oil drained or seen at the fill plug

proof_requests: Photo of the nameplate showing rating and ratio
Clip of the reducer turning under power or by hand, showing the output shaft
Tape measure across the flange and output shaft
Photo of the oil at the fill plug
response.reason: The photos show a cycloidal gear reducer with a cast iron housing, so it can be priced as a not working unit of unknown rating until a nameplate and a running clip are shown.
